To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the dissociation of hydrogen on the Pd (100), surface occurs through a non-activated path, while desorption is a strongly activated process, and that the rotational degrees of freedom of hydrogen have a strong influence on the dissociation dynamics, while the vibrational degrees of the freedom of hydrogen are only weakly coupled to the dissociative adsorptive dynamics.

(a) The dissociation dynamics of the H2 molecule at Pd(100) is characterized by a broad distribution of reaction barriers and a strong coupling between translational and rotational degrees of freedom.

the dissociative adsorptions of H2/Pd(100) and the associative desorption of D2/Pd(111) are both characterized by a strong coupling of the rotational and vibrational motion of the molecule with the translational degrees of freedom, which leads to a significant enhancement of the reaction probability for certain initial conditions of the molecule.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dynamics of the interaction of H 2 with the surface of a Pd (100).
the dynamics of the hydrogen interaction with a Pd (100)-surface.
the interaction of hydrogen with metal surfaces, in particular with the Pd (100), Ni (111) and Ni (100) surfaces.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the dissociative adsorbtion and associative desorption are not only strongly coupled but also strongly steered processes.
the steering effects are very important for dissociative adsorption of H2 on Pd (100), while they have a smaller influence on associative desorption.
the dissociative adsorptive and associative desorptive processes are strongly affected by the rotational and vibrational motion of the hydrogen molecule.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
dissociative adsorption is strongly steered by the rotational degrees of freedom of H 2, whereas associative desorption is strongly steerable by the translational degrees of freedom.

the dissociative adsorbtion and the associative desorption of hydrogen on Pd(100) is a highly non-adiabatic process, in which the coupling of the rotational, translational and vibrational motion of the hydrogen molecule to the surface degrees of freedom plays an important role.
the coupling between these degrees of freedom is very important in the dissociative and associative processes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the rotational and translational degrees of freedom play a crucial role in the dynamics.
the coupling to the rotational and vibrational motions of the molecule can be as important as the coupling to the translation of the molecule.
the coupling of these degrees of freedom leads to a broadening of the distribution of barrier heights, which is a key ingredient in the coexistence of activated and non-activated adsorption.
